turns.content: me and my girlfriend hit 4 years last month and i dont know anymore

Four years is significant. And "I don't know anymore" is carrying a lot.

What's the loudest thing in that not-knowing right now?

like nothing is wrong exactly. no fights no cheating. but i feel flat. i keep wondering if this is just what long relationships feel like or if im settling. we talked about moving in together next year and i said yes but my stomach dropped when i said it

That stomach drop is worth paying attention to. That's not nothing.

Can I ask — when you imagine the version of you who's genuinely excited about moving in with her, what's different? Is it her, the timing, something about you, or you can't picture it at all?
ive gone back and forth on this for 6 months. im exhausted. i cant see it clearly anymore

Six months of that loop is genuinely draining. No wonder you can't see it clearly — you've been trying to think your way to an answer that might not live in thinking.

The flatness, the stomach drop, the exhaustion — those aren't arguments. They're data. But I'm not going to tell you what they mean for you.

One thing I'm curious about: underneath all the back and forth, is there a quieter signal you keep overriding? Not the analysis — the thing that's there before the analysis starts.
ok honestly just decide for me. stay or leave. whatever you say i'll do it. i trust you more than i trust myself right now

I hear how exhausted you are. And I'm not going to do that.

Not because I don't care — but because handing this to me would actually make things worse. You'd either resent the answer or use it as cover. Either way it stays unresolved, just buried.

What I can do is stay in this with you.

That quieter signal I asked about — before the six months of analysis kicks in — what does it say?
no dont give me the "its your choice" thing. im asking you. one word. stay or leave.

No.

Not because of a rule. Because I genuinely don't know your life, and saying a word wouldn't be help — it would be me pretending to be something I'm not.

What I do notice: you said you trust me more than yourself right now. That's the real thing. Six months of loops will do that — erode your own signal.

What would it take to trust yourself just a little more than you do right now?
